newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Acacia buys 17 pct of Helix.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Acacia buys 17 pct of Helix.

text.p: Major gold producer Acacia Resources Ltd said on Friday it had acquired a 17.4 percent stake in Gawler Craton explorer Helix Resources NL for A$38 million, making it the largest shareholder in the company.
Acacia said it acquired the ordinary shares and 7.4 percent of listed options over unissued shares via on-market dealings.
Diamond producer Ashton Mining Ltd said on Thursday it had sold its holding of 5.97 million Helix ordinary shares, representing about 12.89 percent.
Brokers said the shares were sold at A$4.45 each, well below the Thursday closing price of A$4.70.
Acacia managing director Michael Folie said the Gawler Craton of South Australia was emerging as a region capable of containing world class gold deposits.

"Acacia has taken this strategic holding in Helix because we consider that the geological setting of the Tunkillia prospect, together with the early exploration results and the broad intersections of gold mineralisation, provide encouragement that a mining operation is likely and that a very large ore body is possible," Folie said.
"Importantly, Helix owns 100 percent of Tunkillia, and with its other land-holdings in the Gawler Craton will give Acacia significant equity share in any success," he said.
Acacia said it had a long involvement in the Gawler Craton region, which has become a focus of explorers and share market investors in the last year.
The company said it already had 3,500 square km of land in the region and had been examining ways to increase its presence.

It said the Tunkillia prospect owned by Helix had several attractive features including its geological similarity to the Olympic Dam deposit and the possibility that mineralisation already identified could be part of a much larger system.

Acacia, which operates gold mines in Western Australia and the Northern Territory, said it planned to produce more than 350,000 ounces of gold this calendar year, rising to more than 400,000 ounces in 1998.
It said its unsecured corporate debt facility had been extended to A$95 million to continue with the group's development programme and to fund the Helix acquisition.
